correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the update at the three reachable states. At zero, the same-validation-batch inequality is J>3B/4 and J is Bin(B,1/2); from either endpoint, a proposal can only flip to the other endpoint and its acceptance probability is one half of the strict binomial majority tail. The exact survival product and permanent half-unit loss follow. The binomial-tail geometric-ratio sandwich and uniform Stirling inequalities yield c1 B^-1/2 exp(-IB)<=p_B<=c2 B^-1/2 exp(-IB), with I=D(3/4||1/2). Integral-series tests prove both sharp batch-growth boundaries, including equality. The included independently executable exact-rational verifier exhaustively enumerated 24,564 complete sign patterns across B=1..11 and checked four variable-batch schedules. Computation supports the finite laws; it does not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by independent noisy validation as a purported descent safeguard. The result shows a consequential noninterpolating failure: with fixed batch it leaves an *exact* strongly convex optimum almost surely and retains a permanent objective gap, even though every accepted step appears strictly improving on fresh validation data. The exact all-time protection criterion, dimensionless KL slope 7.64455..., sharp additional half-log-log boundary, and high-confidence additive-budget construction answer a natural validation-cost design question that finite-horizon analyses cannot resolve. These are structurally related, not arbitrary isolated parameter slices.
